mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals an active monetary easing cycle that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate lower borrowing costs for corporations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods with three consecutive months of declining FEDFUNDS, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.0% for two consecutive months, it signals persistent labor market weakness that triggers anticipatory monetary stimulus, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors price in policy support.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances with UNRATE > 5.0% for two consecutive months, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rise in unemployment (UNRATE > 5.0%) and decline in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.10%) signals active monetary policy response to labor market deterioration, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days as the market prices in stimulus-driven earnings support.
regime_hint: monetary policy response to labor stress
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods meeting both conditions, or interaction term Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion regimes with strong consumer spending (RSAFS growth > 0.5% monthly) and elevated housing starts (HOUST > 1200), S&P 500 forward returns are positive over 60 days as corporate earnings growth accelerates amid robust demand.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of late-cycle expansion periods (RSAFS growth > 0.5% and HOUST > 1200), or regime-specific Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS > 140,000 monthly) signals strong labor market health that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months with PAYEMS > 140,000, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1150 thousand units for two consecutive months, it signals housing sector contraction that reduces consumer spending and economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances with HOUST < 1150 for two consecutive months, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST < 1200) and industrial production (INDPRO < 105) signals broad economic weakness across consumer and business sectors, generating negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days as corporate profit expectations decline.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods meeting both conditions, or interaction term Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During high industrial growth regimes (INDPRO > 108) with accommodative monetary policy (FEDFUNDS < 0.25%), S&P 500 forward returns are positive over 60 days as manufacturing strength supports earnings and low rates favor equity valuations.
regime_hint: high industrial growth with accommodative policy
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods meeting both conditions, or regime-specific Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.
